objectives: Identify rimes in taught cl-words and familiar CVC partners.
Group words that share the vowel and ending sounds.
Distinguish words that share cl but have different rimes.
Read each word fully after sorting it into a family.
concepts: A word family shares a rime, not necessarily an onset.
Cl-words such as clap, clip, clog, clam and club have different rimes.
Familiar CVC partners such as cap, lip, log, ram and rub help make the rime visible.
Word-family patterns support decoding but do not replace it.

definitions.definition: Words that share a rime, such as clap and cap with -ap.
The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
The initial consonant sound or group before the vowel.

workedExamples.solution: They share -ap; clap has onset cl and cap has onset c.
They share onset cl but have different rimes: -og and -ub.

commonMistakes: Grouping words by onset rather than rime.
Treating all cl-words as one family.
Ignoring the final consonant when sorting.
Guessing from a family label instead of decoding the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to identify a rime.
Words with the same onset can have different rimes.
Words with different onsets can share a rime.
Decode each full word after sorting.
revisionPoints: clam and ram share -am; club and rub share -ub.

basic.prompt: What is the rime in clip?

conceptual.prompt: What makes clap and cap a word-family pair?
Do clog and club share a rime?
conceptual.answer: No; they share cl but have -og and -ub.

conceptual.prompt: Why should you decode after sorting?
conceptual.answer: The family pattern helps but does not replace reading the whole word.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How are clip and lip alike and different?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They share -ip; clip has onset cl and lip has onset l.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why are clap and clip in different rime groups?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Their vowel and ending differ: -ap and -ip.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What should you do if a word does not sound like its family?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Decode it again and check each grapheme.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in clog?
What does a word-family sort help you notice?
mixedReview.answer: Shared rimes and differences among words

activities.name: Sort cl-words by rime.
steps: Read clap, clip, clog, clam and club.
Pair each with a familiar CVC word sharing its rime.
Name the onset and rime in each word.
Read every word again to confirm the sort.

activities.name: Compare cl-words with similar rimes.
steps: Contrast clog/club to hear the vowel and ending difference.
Explain why the onset alone cannot identify the word.

outcomes: Identify onset and rime in taught cl-words.
Explain differences among cl-words with the same onset.
Decode the full word after sorting.

answerKeys.explanation: Clap and cap both end with -ap.
Lip and clip share the -ip rime.
Clam has onset cl and rime -am.
Both begin with cl but have different rimes.
The vowel and ending distinguish cl-words.
Clog and log share the -og rime.

Reading every grapheme confirms the word and the sort.
